https://www.politico.eu/article/vladimir.text: Russia bombarded Ukraine with North Korean missiles overnight, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The Russian attack killed six people and injured at least 19 in Zaporizhzhia, said the city’s mayor, Rehina Kharchenko. Four apartment buildings and several non-residential buildings were damaged in the southeastern city, Kharchenko wrote on her Telegram channel . According to Zelenskyy, the city was struck with North Korean ballistic missiles, Zircons and guided aerial bombs. In a post on X , he wrote: “It was a vicious attack, calculated to inflict maximum damage specifically on civilian infrastructure.” Advertisement Advertisement Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean ruler Kim Jong Un have deepened ties since the Kremlin’s war on Ukraine began. In September last year during a meeting in Beijing, Kim vowed to do “everything we can to assist Russia.” Zelenskyy also reported attacks on a Kyiv hospital and businesses overnight, with at least one person injured. The capital’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko, urged residents late Monday to seek shelter. Moscow also attacked substations in Kherson and Kharkiv, causing power outages, Zelenskyy said. Further attacks took place in the Donetsk, Dnipro and Mykolaiv regions. “Every step Russia takes — increasing ballistic missile production, bringing in North Korean equipment, preparing for mobilization — all of this shows that Moscow is preparing not for peace, but for escalation,” Zelenskyy wrote. Russia has stepped up its missile attacks this summer, with Zelenskyy urging Western allies to help Kyiv strengthen its air defenses and to heap sanctions pressure on companies fueling Moscow’s war. However, Europe is running out of Patriot interceptors to shoot down Russian missiles, according to the continent’s military officials . Ukraine, meanwhile, has struck back, targeting Russian infrastructure including oil refineries and buildings belonging to e-commerce giant Wildberries. Russian state media on Tuesday reported that two Wildberries warehouses in the Voronezh region, several hundred kilometers south of Moscow, caught fire following drone strikes, killing one person. https://www.budapesttimes.hu/hungary/no-.text: The Budapest Times No Hungarians reported among victims of Spain train crash The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has no information about any Hungarian casualties or fatalities in connection with Wednesday's train accident in Spain, the ministry said in a Facebook post. The ministry noted that on Wednesday morning in Spain, two high-speed trains collided on the Madrid–Seville line in the province of Toledo. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that firefighters from Alcázar de San Juan and Orgaz, civil defense personnel from several surrounding towns, three rescue helicopters, and two mobile intensive care units are working at the scene. According to reports, the number of fatalities as a result of the accident currently stands at 46, and this figure may rise further. The ministry stated that no reports have so far been received by the consular office in Madrid in connection with the accident, and that they have no information about any Hungarian casualties or fatalities. They are monitoring the situation and will provide further information if any Hungarian nationals are found to be involved. https://www.dw.com/en/pakistani-astronau.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PnB4 Prefer DW on Google Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali (left) is set to become the first foreigner to join a Chinese space mission Image: Tingshu Wang/REUTERS Advertisement China on Tuesday unveiled the crew for this week's Shenzhou-24 space mission, with a Pakistani payload specialist set to become the first foreign astronaut to board its Tiangong space station . The China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) said that Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a 40-year-old former Pakistani air force pilot, would join two Chinese colleagues when the mission launches from the Jiuquan launch center in China's northwestern Gobi Desert at 8:18 a.m. local time (0018 GMT) on Wednesday. "I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis," Ali told a news conference on Tuesday, switching between Urdu, Mandarin and English. "To every child who is watching while I'm in orbit, just look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams," he said. Pakistan's first astronaut to fly with China To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Pakistan: 'Source of joy and pride' Pakistani officials welcomed Ali's selection as a significant milestone in relations between Islamabad and Beijing who are this year marking 75 years of cooperation in space. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described the mission as a "source of joy and pride for the entire nation" and Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the mission underscored the "iron brotherhood" between the two countries. "This mission is not a finish line; I hope the next chapter of China-Pakistan space cooperation will grow from one astronaut and one flight to multiple joint flights, to the Moon , to Mars , and beyond ," said Ali. "Together with my Chinese crew mates, I will show that this friendship is real, not only on paper, but also in orbit." Muhammad Zeeshan Ali (left) will accompany two Chinese colleagues on the mission Image: Xinhua/dpa/picture alliance What will Pakistani astronaut Ali do in space? Ali will not be the first Pakistani in space, with Monaco-based polar explorer Namira Salim having flown on Virgin Galactic 's Galactic 04 mission in October 2023. But he will be the first foreign astronaut to join a Chinese mission. During a short orbital flight expected to last around five days, Ali will carry out a series of experiments in the fields of biotechnology and photosynthetic microorganisms before returning to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft, which docked at the Tiangong in May. China has poured billions of dollars into its space program. Its prized Tiangong space station is stewarded by teams of three astronauts that are typically rotated every six months. Beijing is aiming to land Chinese astronauts on the moon for the first time by 2030 and is seen as the main space rival to the United States , which is hoping to return to the lunar surface in 2028.
